why.rationale: The narration band is the right move — it adds a human voice above the machine grade without dethroning the exit code. Most responses land warm: the 'Try this first' block has good weight, the human verdict line gives the script a closing breath, and the §-ref dimming lets the eye relax. Two spots still run cold: the 'mid-cycle' subcommand asks the operator to know to type `status`, which is the same cold-start problem one layer up; and the tmux sleep+banner is honest but adds drag — the rhythm sags right where the operator is most anxious. Overall the cluster converges, with one residual seam worth seeding into the next-cycle PRD.
decisions_considered: narration warmth vs exit-code sovereignty — narration wins without displacing
weight of a 'Try this first' block above Options — feels grounding, not patronizing
rhythm cost of a 2sec sleep before FIFO — honest but draggy
discoverability of a status subcommand the cold operator doesn't know exists
mood of dimmed §-refs — receding hum vs invisible scaffolding
